mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases both interest rates and input costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo moving average AND CPIAUCSL > 12mo moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12mo moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a contradictory signal indicating labor market churning; this ambiguity increases market uncertainty and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions within the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of high inflation.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 0.5% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 grows above 0.5% monthly for six consecutive months and CPIAUCSL annual growth is below 2.5%.
